item.title: How China buried Tibet flood images after Nepal disaster
item.description: In Tibet, a digital crackdown followed the deadly flood that has devastated communities along the China-Nepal border. Censors erased viral footage while Chinese state media flooded platforms with official content.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Deceived and deployed: How young Cameroonians end up fighting in Russia's war in Ukraine
item.description: Analysts say economic desperation and fraudulent recruitment schemes are funneling Cameroonian youth into the Russian military — with deadly consequences.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Tariffs spat: Carney bets Canada can defy Trump
item.description: Canada is facing new US import penalties after Prime Minister Mark Carney refused to match US tariffs on China. Other countries are watching as the Trump trade clash turns into a fight over economic sovereignty.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Putin-Modi meeting at SCO: Can Russia-India ties hold?
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Modi and Russian President Putin are at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Kyrgyzstan as Moscow and New Delhi face rising tensions with Washington.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Nepal floods test PM Balen's young government
item.description: A year after Gen Z-led protests swept Prime Minister Balendra "Balen" Shah to power, deadly floods are testing his government's ability to manage a national crisis.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Niger's failed coup exposes cracks in the military — and Russia's influence
item.description: The failed coup in Niger has brought deep divisions within the military to light. As Russia's support highlights the junta's fading influence, soldiers continue to face jihadi attacks, poor equipment and little pay.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Guinea-Bissau votes to reshape presidency
item.description: The West African nation's military government wants to amend the constitution to give more powers to the president. The junta, which seized power last year, says it will hold elections in December.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Greece, Turkey clash over protected Aegean marine areas
item.description: Turkey has announced the creation of two protected zones in a disputed area of the Aegean Sea, sparking an angry reaction from Greece. Does this mark a new chapter in a long-running dispute between the two countries?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: India's citizen-led school audits test limits of activism
item.description: The student-led "Cockroach" movement is taking its campaign for accountability to government schools, but the activists' methods are encountering growing resistance from authorities.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Nepal issues fresh flood warning as 3,000 still missing
item.description: Rescuers are trying to reach dozens of hydropower workers trapped in flooded tunnels, but have been hampered by further rainfall.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinian homes in West Bank
item.description: Masked Israeli settlers launched their first major attack since initiating a siege in the village of Qusra earlier this month. Saturday's attacks were met with rare criticism from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
